newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade quiet, no sales-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade quiet, no sales-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets on Tuesday were quiet, with no sales reported as packer bids at $65.00 to $66.00 per cwt were passed by owners seeking $68.00 to $69.00, feedlot sources said.
"I would expect $67.00 will trade Wednesday on firm beef, but large showlists could keep prices from going to $68.00," said Dale Benson, livestock analyst with Dean Witter Reynolds.
The bulk of sales last week occured at $68.00 before prices slipped to $67.00 in light trade Thursday and Friday.
Closing boxed beef prices Tuesday were quoted up $0.13 to $0.31 per cwt on 264 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
Feedlots in the Texas Panhandle were quickly drying following mixed heavy rain and snow last Friday, with the hardest hit areas of Hereford and Amarillo almost dried out.
"Today, for the first time since the storm, I saw dust kicked up behind a truck after it passed by," a Panhandle-area feedyard manager said.
